summary: Milestone of 2026-10-30/31 (latest): behaviour explanation v2 (E32) and a phone-sized behaviour encoder (E33). E32 was developed on the E31 collection only and frozen (3f8eae9): feature version 2 (gap bridging, track holding, context detections), a turning-in-place window model for tail chasing, hiss/growl as threat evidence, recording context (person near, objects, sounds, place) with half the weight of the user's words, before/after events, parser v2 (after/before/until context phrases, MiniLM paraphrase matching), knowledge base v2 (21 behaviours, 33 sources incl. neurological look-alikes). Pre-registered test (0402c46) on 37 fresh clips and questions, scored once, paired with the frozen E31 system: v2 better over all questions (asked behaviours recognized 24 vs 21/33, parse 16 vs 13/33, request separation 28 vs 25/33, expert interpretation covered 6 vs 3/7, ranked first 5 vs 1/7; tail chasing 2/2 vs 1/2 with confusers 2/2), but post hoc only through the five questions on conditions knowledge base v2 was extended for after the test papers were chosen (on the other 32 the systems tie on every explanation check; recognition 20 vs 21 of 28) but parse (0.48) and request separation (0.85) stay below 0.9, so by the fixed rule the default stays the E31 system (kept verbatim in understand/e31, verified to reproduce the tested answers); v2 via --system-version 2. Post-hoc: fresh paraphrases defeat the parser; new behaviours at the fixed threshold fire on unrelated clips; the recording context over-reports people. E33 (pre-registered): a MobileNetV3-Large student distilled from SigLIP on 20k cat/dog crops reaches zero-shot macro AP 0.273 vs 0.416 on the E31 pool (retains 58 % above chance; bar 80 % not met; not adopted); its 4-15 MB exports run bit-exact (float) in desktop headless Chromium at 15-48 ms per crop. E34: off-the-shelf TinyCLIP 8M / 39M reach 0.267 / 0.308 (not adopted). Previous milestone (2026-10-20): E31 explanation in context, G1b detector. Not on the phone; phones remain untested.

decisions: The phone test build uses the licence-stated TF Hub detector. Q-M2 was answered on 2026-10-19: the MediaPipe Object Detector page states no licence for the weights, so the MediaPipe detector stays research-only. On home phone video (E20) the TF Hub detector is the better one anyway.

Only vocalization types that passed the pre-set FSD50K gate (meow, bark) are shown or open/support interpretations; unvalidated confident types (purr, growl, hiss) remain in the JSON and can only block an interpretation (E21).
The on-furniture relation ships as the pre-specified containment rule; the learned head was not better (E15 follow-up).
Dog keypoints, MammalNet-trained heads, the AwA-Pose cat keypoint heads and the bark-context model stay research-only (data terms).
Server analysis is opt-in; the default path never uploads media.

resources_needed: Run the phone test on one iPhone and one Android phone
A Kaggle API token for CatFLW / DogFLW (cat and dog facial landmarks, research)
Annotators for G2 (70-100 h for 2,000 cats + 2,000 dogs), or a per-image licence check of the AwA2 cat and dog images used by E24
Household recordings: participants and a data controller (docs/household/CONSENT_AND_PRIVACY.md)
An HTTPS host with header control for the installed-app track (only after track A)

Owner-written questions about their own recordings (with consent) for the behaviour-explanation benchmark: the assistant-written E31/E32 questions flattered the parser (E32 C1 0.48 on fresh paraphrases)
Behaviour-rich cat and dog video with terms that allow training (drinking, kneading, grooming, tail chasing) to distil a phone-sized behaviour encoder; E33/E34 show generic photos are not enough
Cat video frames for the next detector candidate: G1b gains dogs on real video but not cats (acceptance 2)
